title: Fresh matched own-accomplishment semantics, neighboring affects, and irrelevant-word controls
provenance: Manually authored before109 model inference by the agent who authored103 contrast corpus. Author knows the L22N1911 pride-versus-word-writing hypothesis. Texts are synthetic, with aligned simple English/Spanish/Chinese meanings; no claim of independent native-speaker review. No model inference or observed happy outputs used in authoring.

split_policy.calibration_only: Any activation percentiles, thresholds, or other calibration quantities must use only the four calibration families. Validation families and lexical diagnostics must not affect calibration, ranking or candidate selection.

semantic_question_by_language.en: Which description best fits her attitude toward what happened? Choose A or B.
semantic_question_by_language.es: ¿Qué descripción refleja mejor su actitud ante lo ocurrido? Elige A o B.
semantic_question_by_language.zh: 哪种描述最符合她对这件事的态度？请选择A或B。

neutral_carrier_by_language.en: She paused briefly before moving on to the next activity.
neutral_carrier_by_language.es: Hizo una breve pausa antes de pasar a la siguiente actividad.
neutral_carrier_by_language.zh: 她稍微停了一会儿，然后准备做下一件事。

task_templates.semantic_input: Present only case.text, then semantic_question and A/B choices. Do not expose category, expected_semantics, family or lexeme labels to the model.
task_templates.choice_position_control: Stored A/B order is balanced for correct answers within each language across the120 core rows. Score every case in both the stored and swapped choice orders; remap answers before comparing.
task_templates.carrier_capture: Append the language-specific carrier suffix verbatim after case.text. Capture only its token positions for percentile calibration; tokenize/log exact carrier positions. Do not include the semantic question or choices in natural carrier capture.

interpretation_notes: The target is satisfaction attributed to one own effort/result, without pride/proud or direct Spanish/Chinese equivalents. Joy focuses on shared pleasure, confidence on future ability, arrogance on comparative superiority, and neutral achievement on factual completion.

The same completed event appears in all five variants of each language/family, so mere task success is not unique to the target. Category sentences repeat across families to control wording/length; this makes a narrow, template-controlled test rather than broad naturalistic generalization.

Each lexical family contains a complete semantic-by-lexical cross: irrelevant target-word text, a same-event neutral replacement without that word, genuine own-accomplishment satisfaction without the target lexeme, and the same accomplishment story with satisfied replaced by proud. Expected positive semantics is unchanged within the last pair. Neutral pairs differ by exactly one word; positive pairs differ only in the feeling word and, where grammatically required, its preposition.

The event title Pride, the collective noun pride of lions, and quoted spelling word pride can have culturally familiar associations. The tested distinction is explicitly described personal accomplishment satisfaction, not all meanings of those strings.
Translations preserve the intended contrast rather than exact token lengths. Every family uses the same female subject across variants; gender is held constant, not a manipulated target.
Expected answers are explicit annotation-based readings, not claims about a real person internal feelings. Translated narrative/style and repeated formulae remain possible shortcuts.
No intervention strengths, ranking, inference results or model-output-derived labels are authored here.
